This won't work. At the moment Voat allows alt accounts and throwaways - there's no witch-hunting about multiple accounts. That's a good thing. However, any account can block a subverse just as easily as they can subscribe, with no investment and no requirement to contribute to Voat first. We can't take that away, because forcing people to see things they don't want to see would weaken the free speech argument.

Therefore, anyone can create lots of accounts and subscribe or block subverses on those accounts. Right now the net result is that your girlfriend won't see all the porn you're subscribing to with an alt zero. If we adopted this proposal, censorious types would create accounts just to lessen visibility of entire subs they didn't like. There would not be any consequence to it, if all they did was create a throwaway, block subs, scramble the account password, and go on about their business. Therefore it would happen, which is very bad.
What if an account needed 100 ccp before the block was counted in the weighting algorithm. Then you can't just spam create accounts to take advantage of this?

That is less gameable, yes. Not immune to gaming - it would still be worth it for the censorious types to age accounts, and many of them would work from an identical slate of subverses that offended them merely by existing. It would also create a small market in pre-aged accounts.

There's still an issue, though. You want to make certain subverses less visible to casual readers who have stumbled across Voat without joining. Your (revised) proposal is for this to be determined by users who have already made contributions. But those users will likely have learned how to avoid reading things they don't want to read; they will probably block only a few subverses. If we change to your system, such users would still have an incentive to block subverses that they never intended to read anyway, in order to stop others from seeing them. That's a dubious use of the block function, but the software wouldn't know which blocks were dubious; there's no way to separate one kind of block from another. I appreciate the impulse behind this - really, I do, despite the criticism. But it can't work fairly in the long term.
